sonnet.q1: The monolith notifications row, written by enqueue_notification inside the business caller's own transaction, is the first durable record. It exists only if that transaction commits.
sonnet.q2: The broker is at-least-once: it redelivers any message not acked within 30 s, possibly to another consumer instance.
sonnet.q3: 5 tries total, with backoff of 1, 2, 4, then 8 minutes between attempts (attempts+1, next_attempt_at = now + delay). On the 5th failure the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: One type at a time: shipping_update, then order_confirmed, then password_reset, each at least 3 days on the new service before the next (order_confirmed after shipping_update has had 3 days of passing checks, with p99 recorded). Before password_reset moves: order_confirmed has had 3 days on notif-svc AND its p99 is under 60 s; otherwise fix latency and don't flip.
sonnet.q5: idempotency_key=notification_id. It is the UUID that enqueue_notification makes (row.id in the old worker's _deliver). MailRelay drops the repeat (it remembers keys for 24 h) and returns success, so the row is marked sent and only one email goes out.
sonnet.q6: Via the outbox relay/publisher in the monolith: it polls every 1 s for route='service', status='pending' rows, publishes each to the notifications.requested broker topic, waits for broker confirmation, sets status published and commits. The notif-svc listener consumes it. The monolith is done once the row is published; it never sends email or retries sends.
sonnet.q7: enqueue_notification decides, at enqueue time, by reading the flag notify.route.<type> inside the caller's transaction and writing it to the row's route column (monolith if the flag read fails). The route is set once and never changed.
sonnet.q8: The ledger's deliveries table has notification_id as primary key, and the listener does INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (notification_id) DO NOTHING, so a duplicate does nothing and is just acked. Also MailRelay's idempotency key protects against repeat sends.
sonnet.q9: The service acks after committing the ledger insert and before anything is sent. A crash before the commit: the message is redelivered after 30 s. A crash between commit and ack: the redelivery's insert does nothing and it is just acked.
sonnet.q10: In the service's own ledger (deliveries table: status, attempts, next_attempt_at). The notif-svc sender acts on it, polling every 1 s for up to 50 pending rows with next_attempt_at <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
sonnet.q11: Rolling back is the flag going back to monolith. Already service-routed rows keep their route: they still go through the outbox publisher and are sent by notif-svc, since the publisher and service keep running. Nothing is lost or sent twice. New rows go to the old worker.
sonnet.q12: The message carries notification_id, type, email, payload and created_at. The email content is rendered in notif-svc, where the templates live.
